proposed_widenings.name: class_spellcasting_framework
proposed_widenings.justification: No existing mechanics family captures the installation of a class's full spellcasting infrastructure: spell slot economy, prepared-spell list management, spellcasting ability assignment, and focus grant. The `passive` family with `grants` is designed for specific EffectAtom bundles; no EffectAtom covers 'grant access to the Sorcerer spell list at N prepared spells per level'. The `activation` family requires use-count + reset cadence, which doesn't model a passive framework install.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. [...] Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Sorcerer spells.

proposed_widenings.name: grant_spell_slots
proposed_widenings.justification: Spell slots are a class-level resource economy (table-driven, refill on Long Rest) distinct from the `use_count` + `charge_pool` resources modeled for activated abilities. There is no EffectAtom or resource atom that expresses 'grant a slot table keyed to class level with Long Rest reset'.
proposed_widenings.evidence: The Sorcerer Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

proposed_widenings.name: set_spellcasting_ability
proposed_widenings.justification: No EffectAtom sets which ability score is used as the spellcasting ability modifier for a class's spell attack rolls and spell save DCs. `set_ability_score` sets the score value; `modify_ability_score` adjusts it — neither designates an ability as the casting stat for the class framework.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Sorcerer spells.

proposed_widenings.name: grant_class_spell_list_access
proposed_widenings.justification: `grant_spell_access` grants access to a specific named spell by `spellId`. It cannot express 'may prepare any N spells from the Sorcerer spell list, where N scales with class level'. This requires a spell-list reference plus a scaling prepared-count, neither of which the current surface supports.
proposed_widenings.evidence: choose two level 1 Sorcerer spells [...] The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Sorcerer levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Sorcerer Features table.

notes: All five sub-features (cantrips, spell slots, prepared spells, spellcasting ability, spellcasting focus) are parts of a unified class spellcasting framework. None map to existing EffectAtoms or mechanics families. `grant_spell_access` handles individual named spells; it cannot represent open-ended list access with level-scaled prepared counts. No content file produced — forcing this into `passive` grants would require fabricating atom kinds the tracer would reject.
